title: Evasion
summary: Evasion is the set of techniques used to avoid, delay or defeat detection and analysis rather than to achieve an objective directly, and it is best understood as a tax on defenders' visibility rather than a single action. Practitioners group it by what is being evaded: signature matching, behavioural analytics, logging, and human investigation. Common patterns include altering the on-disk representation of code so known signatures no longer match, obfuscating scripts and command lines, abusing signed system utilities so actions appear under a trusted name, masquerading files and services as legitimate software, tampering with or blinding telemetry so evidence never reaches a central store, and encrypting or tunnelling command-and-control traffic so content inspection becomes useless. Because evasion targets the collection layer, the most effective counters are architectural. Centralised, append-only logging with strict access control removes the advantage of tampering on a single host. Tamper protection and health monitoring on endpoint agents expose attempts to disable them. Application control and script block logging shrink the space in which obfuscated code can run at all. Behavioural detections that correlate across hosts and identities survive cosmetic changes better than any signature. Finally, analysts should treat absence of evidence as a signal in itself: a host that stops reporting, a log source that goes quiet, or a gap in a timeline is a detection opportunity, and treating those gaps as alerts is one of the highest-value habits a security operations team can build.
objectives: You will be able to classify evasion techniques by whether they target signatures, behaviour, logging or investigation.
You will be able to identify signs that telemetry has been disabled, blinded or tampered with.
You will be able to explain why centralised, append-only logging defeats many host-level evasion tactics.
You will be able to design behavioural detections that survive cosmetic changes to tooling.
You will be able to treat monitoring gaps and silent hosts as actionable detection signals.

beginner.definition: Evasion means changing how an attack looks so that security tools do not notice it. It does not achieve the goal by itself. Instead it delays or prevents detection, giving the intruder more time. Evasion targets many things: file signatures, behaviour patterns, logging, and the humans who investigate alerts.
beginner.whyItMatters: Security tools are only useful if they can see what is happening. Evasion attacks that visibility directly. An intruder may rename tools, hide inside trusted programs, or switch off logging on one machine. If your logs live only on that machine, the evidence disappears with them. Central logging and tamper protection keep the record safe. Treat a silent host as a warning sign, not as peace and quiet.
howItWorks: The intruder studies which security tools watch the machines they want to use.
They change their tools so that known detection patterns no longer match.
They hide their actions inside trusted programs that already run on the system.
They try to turn off, blind or delete the logging on the affected machine.
If detection is delayed, they gain quiet time to reach their real goal.
beginner.example: Think of a burglar who puts on a delivery driver's uniform. The neighbours see a familiar van and a friendly wave. Nothing about the scene feels wrong, so nobody calls the police. The uniform did not open the door by itself. It simply stopped people from looking too closely. Malicious activity that hides behind trusted system tools works the same way. The lesson for defenders is to watch behaviour, not just names and appearances.
takeaways: Evasion does not attack your data, it attacks your ability to see.
Send logs to a central place that intruders cannot edit.
A host that stops reporting is a signal worth chasing.

exercises.title: Evasion - EASY
exercises.summary: Recall and recognition: definitions, one clear answer, single-step questions.

exercises.title: Evasion - MEDIUM
exercises.summary: Application: read a short log or alert and choose the correct next step.

exercises.title: Evasion - HARD
exercises.summary: Analysis: a multi-step scenario with distractors, evidence to weigh, and a reason to give.

exercises.title: Evasion - EXTREMELY HARD
exercises.summary: Synthesis under pressure: incomplete evidence, competing priorities, and a decision you must defend.
